newsitem.title: CANADA: Conciliator gives up on Inco labor dispute.
newsitem.headline: Conciliator gives up on Inco labor dispute.

text.p: A conciliator sent by the government of Manitoba to settle a labor dispute at Inco Ltd's Manitoba facility has left, the company and union said.
The two sides were too far apart to make conciliation worthwhile, spokesmen for Inco and the United Steelworkers said in separate interviews.
"It just wasn't possible," said Inco spokesman Dan McSweeney. "We're far apart on the outstanding issues."
Inco locked out about 1,400 unionized workers on Sunday after the union voted to reject Inco's final contract offer.
Shift scheduling and wages are the main stumbling blocks.
Inco produces about 100 million pounds of nickel a year from the Thompson area in northern Manitoba, or 20 percent of Inco's total output.
There were no plans for further talks, but both sides said they were willing to negotiate.
"We are willing. Give us a call and say where and when," said Nelson Pruder, a spokesman for local 6166 of the United Steelworkers of America.
Analysts estimate that Thompson accounts for about 5.6 percent of the world's nickel supply.
